correctness.rationale: For all primes p>=11, the binary log weights obey w_j<=tail_j: small j by five exact product inequalities and all j>=10 via the published prime-ratio bound, an induction-by-contradiction and the prime number theorem. Therefore the squarefree tail subset-products fill [1,T] in closure, while higher exponents stay inside. Four head-prime exponent bounds reduce the remaining possibilities to 135 intervals. The exact rational standalone verifier establishes identical 14-component partitions for the two analytic enclosures T_-<T<T_+, yielding all endpoints and strict gaps. It checks finite premises but does not assert the ratio lemma or PNT by experiment.

value.rationale: Defant explicitly posed component-count sets E_k^*. The cubic parameter gives a naturally motivated exact new point E_14^*, with fourteen fully specified intervals and thirteen certified open gaps. The sharp value and rigorous finite reduction are nontrivial and not an arbitrary numerical cutoff. The result complements the previously published two-component case at t=-2 and clarifies the topology of a canonical arithmetic-function image.
